item: Commercial Litigation cluster - M-2013 (Harmon & Slate), M-2014 (Whitfield Bosch), M-2015 (Dunmore Ellery Pratt), M-2016 (Castellan Vega)
driver: All four Commercial Litigation matters, across four different firms, were staffed 84-100% by partner hours with little to no associate leverage (M-2014 and M-2015 used zero associate hours at all), unlike every other matter type in the panel, which runs on associate/paralegal hours with partners contributing only oversight-level time.
recommendation: Require associate-level staffing for discovery and motion-practice phases in future litigation engagement letters panel-wide; ask each firm for a staffing-plan justification on the four matters above.

item: Regulatory and Tax Advisory matter types (M-2007, M-2012 Regulatory; M-2002, M-2011, M-2022 Tax Advisory)
driver: Partner-hour share is consistent across firms and matters within each type (roughly 30-38% for Tax Advisory, 55% for Regulatory), suggesting purposeful, not outlier, staffing.
recommendation: No staffing action needed; use these ratios as the internal benchmark when reviewing new engagement letters for these matter types.

item: Real Estate and IP/Licensing matter types (M-2008, M-2009, M-2021 Real Estate; M-2003, M-2004, M-2005, M-2019 IP/Licensing)
driver: Consistently associate/paralegal-driven with minimal-to-no partner hours across every instance in the dataset -- no outliers.
recommendation: No action needed; this is the staffing model to hold up as the standard for these matter types.

item: Commercial Litigation cluster total: $302,330 billed vs. $145,000 budgeted
driver: Directly tied to the partner-heavy staffing pattern above; M-2014 overran +153.5%, M-2015 +135.8%, M-2013 +86.4%, M-2016 +73.7% -- a 4-for-4 miss rate that points to a broken estimating process for this matter type, not isolated firm behavior.
recommendation: Rebuild the litigation intake/budgeting process with a complexity questionnaire before a budget number is set for the next matter.

item: M-2018 Employment Matter (Reyes Chen Kaplan): $31,500 vs $18,000 budget
driver: Direct consequence of the partner-only staffing flagged above -- a 75% overrun ($13,500 excess) on work that should be routine.
recommendation: Tie the staffing conversation with Reyes Chen Kaplan to a firm commitment on future employment-matter rate/staffing before assigning more of this work.

item: M-2007 Regulatory Matter (Whitfield Bosch): $14,070 vs $12,000 budget
driver: A modest 17.25% overrun consistent with the matter type's normal partner-heavy staffing; not clearly a staffing problem but worth a one-line check with the firm on scope.
recommendation: Confirm with Whitfield Bosch whether scope expanded mid-matter before renewing the estimate for similar Regulatory work.

item: M-2017 M&A Matter (Castellan Vega): $58,800 vs $55,000 budget
driver: Small 6.9% overrun; the more significant issue on this matter is the missing partner hours (see Staffing Mix), not the modest cost variance.
recommendation: Address via the partner-review-step action above; no separate budget action needed.

item: Systemic underrun pattern - 15 of 22 matters (all Tax Advisory, Real Estate, IP/Licensing, and standard Employment matters) came in 10-27% under budget
driver: Consistent underrun across matter types and firms suggests estimates are set with a conservative cushion rather than being tightly calibrated -- not a cost problem, but a scoping-accuracy question worth confirming is intentional.
recommendation: Confirm with legal ops whether the cushion in these estimates is deliberate; if not, tighten estimating guidance for these matter types.

item: Commercial Litigation assignment across the whole panel (Harmon & Slate, Whitfield Bosch, Dunmore Ellery Pratt, Castellan Vega)
driver: The same overstaffing/overrun pattern shows up at all four firms that handled a litigation matter, even though those firms staff their other matter types very differently -- this points to a panel-wide intake/staffing convention for litigation, not one firm's behavior.
recommendation: Treat this as a process fix (litigation intake and staffing plan requirements) rather than a single-firm renegotiation.

item: Reyes Chen Kaplan - IP/Licensing specialist assigned one Employment matter (M-2018)
driver: Reyes Chen Kaplan handled 3 IP/Licensing matters efficiently (all under budget, standard associate/paralegal staffing) but its one Employment matter is the worst outlier in the dataset -- consistent with being assigned work outside its demonstrated specialty without an appropriate associate bench.
recommendation: Route future Employment matters to a firm with a demonstrated Employment-practice bench rather than this firm's IP team.

item: Castellan Vega LLP - broadest matter-type spread in the panel (Tax Advisory, Regulatory, Commercial Litigation, M&A, Real Estate)
driver: As the most generalist firm in the panel, Castellan Vega sits at both ends of the allocation-imbalance spectrum: the zero-partner-hours M&A matter (M-2017) and one of the four overstaffed litigation matters (M-2016) -- breadth of assignment may be outrunning depth of bench in specific matter types.
recommendation: Review whether Castellan Vega's M&A and litigation staffing plans reflect a genuine specialty bench before routing more of that work to them.

item: Whitfield Bosch M&A matter (M-2006) as a staffing benchmark
driver: This matter shows appropriate partner-to-associate-to-paralegal leverage (20%/55%/25% of hours) and came in under budget -- a useful positive benchmark rather than a problem.
recommendation: Reference this staffing ratio when negotiating M&A staffing plans with other panel firms.

item: Real Estate work concentration (Dunmore Ellery Pratt x2, Castellan Vega x1)
driver: Staffed consistently (associate + paralegal only, no partner hours) across all three matters and both firms, and all came in at or under budget -- looks like appropriate specialization, no allocation concern.
